previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, bipolar disorder, and a history of pseudoseizures was readmitted for severe right-sided abdominal pain worsened by a fall, following a recent discharge. He reported inability to tolerate oral intake and had a seizure likely due to missed medications. Imaging and labs showed no acute abnormalities, with normal lipase and a clear chest X-ray. The hospital course focused on pain control with morphine and Dilaudid, initiation of pancreatic enzymes and omeprazole for exocrine insufficiency, and discontinuation of all antiepileptic drugs after video EEG showed no epileptiform activity, confirming pseudoseizures. His diabetes was managed with reduced-dose NPH insulin, and amitriptyline was started for neuropathic pain. He was advanced to a regular diet, pain was well controlled, and he was discharged home with medication changes and follow-up plans.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled

radiology_notes.text:
CT TORSO DATED ___

HISTORY:  ___ man with chronic pancreatitis and cholelithiasis with
severe worsening abdominal pain after syncopal episode versus seizure.
Clinical concern for dissection.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous helical acquisition through the chest, abdomen, and
pelvis was performed with intravenous contrast.  A CTA was performed to
evaluate integrity of the aorta.  MIP images of the pulmonary arteries were
also obtained in addition to coronal and sagittally reformatted images of the
torso.

FINDINGS:

CTA CHEST:  The heart is top normal in size.  There is atherosclerotic
calcification of the coronary arteries.  The aorta opacifies normally with no
evidence of dissection.  The pulmonary arteries opacify normally with no
evidence of pulmonary embolism.  There is a 1.7-cm right hilar lymph node
identified.  There is no left hilar lymphadenopathy and no mediastinal
lymphadenopathy.  There is no pericardial effusion.  The tracheobronchial tree
is patent to the level of the subsegmental bronchi bilaterally.  There is
bibasilar atelectasis.  No pleural effusions or pneumothorax identified.

CT ABDOMEN:  The liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and bowel are normal in
appearance.  There is a replaced right hepatic artery. There is a hypodense
lesion within the interpolar region of the right kidney which is too small to
characterize but likely represents a renal cyst and unchanged from the prior
study.  The left kidney is normal in appearance.  Gallstones are noted
dependently within the gallbladder.  There is no pericholecystic fluid or
stranding identified. Calcifications are noted throughout the pancreas,
consistent with the patient's history of chronic pancreatitis.  Also noted is
stable pancreatic ductal dilitation. There is no peripancreatic stranding or
fluid identified. There is no free fluid or free air within the abdomen.
Multiple small retroperitoneal lymph nodes are identified which are not
pathologically enlarged by size criterion.

CT PELVIS:  The prostate is normal in appearance.  There is no pelvic mass,
lymphadenopathy, or free fluid.  The visualized bowel is normal in appearance.

CT BONE WINDOWS:  The osseous structures are intact without evidence of
fracture or focal lesion.  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions are
identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism or aortic dissection.
2.  Bibasilar atelectasis and an enlarged right hilar lymph node which may be
reactive in nature.
3.  Cholelithiasis without evidence of cholecystitis.
4.  Calcifications of the pancreas which are consistent with the patient's
history of chronic pancreatitis.  No evidence of acute pancreatitis.
